summary: This function creates an interactive SSH launcher that reads your SSH config files, extracts host aliases and their descriptions from comments, displays them in a searchable menu using fzf, and then connects to your chosen host. The description supports colored text formatting in the preview pane to make documentation richer and more scannable.

explanations.34: This pipes your SSH config files through a Perl script that extracts and structures the data. The 2>/dev/null suppresses error messages if some config files don't exist.
explanations.35: Sets up a separator string that will be used to join multiple comment lines together so they appear as one block.
explanations.36: Removes Windows-style line endings and strips the newline at the end of the current line, so the script processes clean text.
explanations.39: Checks if the current line is a comment (starts with # after any whitespace).
explanations.40: Strips the leading # and any space after it from the comment, keeping just the text content.
explanations.42: Adds the comment to a buffer, separating multiple comments with the separator string so they can be joined later.
explanations.47: Looks for a Host line in the config and captures the alias name (the part after 'Host' that isn't a wildcard).
explanations.49: Before storing the new host entry, print out the previous one if it exists, otherwise the last entry would be lost.
explanations.50: Resets variables to start fresh for the new host: stores the new alias, attaches any accumulated description to it, clears the comment buffer, and sets hostname to a default.
explanations.55: Extracts the actual hostname or IP address from the HostName line and stores it.
explanations.64: Creates a long string of spaces; this acts as invisible padding in the fzf list to push the description far to the right so it doesn't clutter the main columns.
explanations.65: Formats each line with fixed-width columns for alias and IP, then adds padding and a delimiter, then the description. The delimiter lets fzf know where to split the data for the preview.
explanations.68: Pre-fills the search box with whatever argument you passed to the sshf function (if any).
explanations.70: Tells fzf to use ##### as the boundary between the display part and the preview data.
explanations.77: The preview shows field 2 (the description part after the delimiter) and converts the color tags into actual ANSI escape codes so the preview displays with colors.
explanations.91: Runs ssh -G to get all the expanded configuration values for the chosen alias, which includes the actual hostname and username after SSH has resolved any inheritance from the config.
explanations.92: Extracts just the username from the full config output by looking for the line that starts with 'user '.
explanations.93: Extracts just the hostname from the full config output by looking for the line that starts with 'hostname '.
explanations.94: Extracts just the first identity file (private key) from the config, since there could be multiple and we only want the first one.
explanations.97: Prints a bold cyan message showing the exact SSH command about to execute, so the user can see what's happening before the connection starts.
